pr_title: shell: uart: Add option to route shell through USB CDC ACM
pr_body:
Addition of a simple way of permitting routing of shell through a USB CDC ACM UART.

Fixes: #26051.

Signed-off-by: Kuba Sanak <contact@kuba.fyi>
pr_comments:
When wanting to route the shell through USB CDC ACM there is a problem with the shell getting possibly initialised before the CDC ACM driver. 

I managed to successfully accomplish what I need by adding a call to `usb_enable()` in the `enable_shell_uart()` function and changing the literal `0` shell initialisation priority to `CONFIG_APPLICATION_INIT_PRIORITY` (so that it happens after the USB device's `CONFIG_KERNEL_INIT_PRIORITY_DEVICE`.

However, I'm not sure if this is the correct way to do it with me being possibly unaware of the reason why shell's initialisation needs to be `0`, an the best place to `usb_enable()` - I'm open to suggestions of better ways of doing it.
Also, the way I defined Kconfig for this option doesn't correctly source the CDC ACM UART device name from its Kconfig value. I'm pretty new to Kconfig so would appreciate any insights on this one.

issue_context.title: shell: uart: Allow a change in the shell initalisation to let routing it through USB UART
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
When wanting to route the shell through USB CDC ACM there is a problem with the shell getting possibly initialised before the CDC ACM driver. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I managed to successfully accomplish what I need by adding a call to `usb_enable()` in the `enable_shell_uart()` function and changing the literal `0` shell initialisation priority to `CONFIG_APPLICATION_INIT_PRIORITY` (so that it happens after the USB device's `CONFIG_KERNEL_INIT_PRIORITY_DEVICE`.

However, I'm not sure if this is the correct way to do it with me being possibly unaware of the reason why shell's initialisation needs to be `0`, an the best place to `usb_enable()`.
comments: I've done the work on my fork at https://github.com/KubaFYI/zephyr/tree/feat_usb_acm_shell.

> I've done the work on my fork at https://github.com/KubaFYI/zephyr/tree/feat_usb_acm_shell.

Why don't you send an RFC PR with the code you have and we then discuss it there?
@carlescufi Oh ok. I always kinda assumed it's annoying to bother everyone with PRs which have not been discussed to be the right way forward, but if that's the preferred workflow I'll go for it!

> @carlescufi Oh ok. I always kinda assumed it's annoying to bother everyone with PRs which have not been discussed to be the right way forward, but if that's the preferred workflow I'll go for it!

No actually, many discussions can take place directly in the PR. Thanks for your contribution!

The solution in current Zephyr tree is to configure the shell (`CONFIG_UART_SHELL_ON_DEV_NAME="CDC_ACM_0"`) and enable USB device support in user application.
See also https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/26122#issuecomment-689417216

review_comments: This might not be right.  If `CONFIG_UART_SHELL_ON_DEV_NAME` and `CONFIG_UART_CONSOLE_ON_DEV_NAME` are both true then the shell would be enabled on the device before the console is enabled (in level `APPLICATION` at priority `CONFIG_UART_CONSOLE_INIT_PRIORITY`).
As described for #27071 this hijacks a call that's supposed to be available to the application to register for USB event status changes.
